comment_data.body:
The `Diff*` highlight groups are for `:h diff-mode`, so the naming doesn't quite fit here.
The `diff*` (and as far as I understand `@diff.*`) highlight groups are for diff patches.

If I understand this correctly, the most fitting solution here is for queries to just use `@diff.plus` and `@diff.minus` captures. This approach:
- Doesn't require new special highlight groups.
- By default would use the already defined diff-patch tree-sitter highlight groups, which would highlight foreground as green and red.
- Opens the door for the user to override as `@diff.plus.diff` and `@diff.minus.diff` to have green and red background if they want to show syntax highlighting in diffs. Those groups also may or may not be defined by the default color scheme in this way.

comment_data.body:
Following [this discussion](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40851#discussion_r3789120471), I still think that defining these groups in default color scheme is a bad idea, assuming the currently laid out workflow of "opt-in via enabling tree-sitter".

The main culprit is that this will immediately break virtually all color schemes in diff files with tree-sitter enabled. Here is what will happen:
- If color scheme does nothing, then `+` / `-` lines will be highlighted with green / red colors that don't match the color scheme. Which usually leads to readability issues, not even mentioning the aesthetic reasons. So color schemes *must* do something here. Which is already bad, especially since color schemes are not the most active plugins.
- It is not quite possible for the color scheme to support both "without injections" and "with injections" use cases. Since the first is usually highlighted via foreground and the second requires background highlighting. And color schemes don't know in advance which variant will be used.
- Also, a significant amount of color schemes don't have a dedicated "green/red background" color in their palette (like, for example, the whole `base16` approach). For `Diff*` groups they use green/red foreground color as background with regular background color as the foreground. So they in principle can't support "highlighted text with colored background" use case, as the foreground from the `@diff.{plus,minus}.diff` groups will be overridden by the injected syntax highlighting.

I would prefer to work on these queries in nvim-treesitter -- we have much better (more specific) CI there. I would also like to keep that as the record of truth without exception (for the same reason)  @ribru17

(It'll take another one or two weeks until I cut another diff parser release anyway, so we don't need to hurry there.)

> Also, the current implementation doesn't seem to 100% work after quick testing. Not all hunks have syntax highlighting. For example, this diff file has only the first hunk with syntax highlighting:

In that example, the diff is technically not syntactically correct (at least, in the eyes of tree-sitter). Context lines always need a preceding space character to be detected, if they're empty then they aren't parsed as part of the parent `hunk`. The space characters should always get inserted by `git --diff` thankfully (and `diff -u`)

My bad, I copied the output of `git show HEAD` from the shell and the extra whitespace did not make it through. With the output of `git show HEAD > test.diff` everything indeed works as expected.

Although it indeed lowers the priority, I don't think it is fair to treat it as "not syntactically correct". The web search didn't show any strict specification about that single whitespace. So at least on "best effort basis" it would be better to support. And if "best effort basis" is "no support since the parser says so", then so be it :)
